title: Modern navigation (Flexbox)
instructions:
Goal:

The navigation bar currently looks broken. Your task is to transform it into a proper header panel.

  • Wrap the (.navbar) so that its children (Logo, Menu, Button) are aligned in a single row.
  • Push these three main elements apart so that there is even spacing between them (one on the left, one in the center, and one on the right)
  • Ensure all elements are vertically centered.
  • The menu (.nav-links) also arrange them in a row and add an appropriate gap (30px) between the links.
solutionCss: .navbar { background-color: white; padding: 15px 30px; border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; } .nav-links { display: flex; gap: 30px; }

checks.message: The main panel must use a one-dimensional model (Flexbox) to arrange the elements.

checks.message: The items are not properly spaced. Use the property that pushes the elements to the maximum edges of the container.
checks.studentHint: The items in the navbar are pushed to the edges.

checks.message: The logo, menu, and button are not aligned. Align them vertically along the center axis.
checks.studentHint: The header content is vertically centered.

checks.message: The links are cramped together. To create a clean space between them, use the property designed for flex/grid containers.
